extracted.intended_audience: corporate sustainability/reporting professionals, investors, ESG/impact analysts, and corporate communications staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and evaluating SASB-aligned sustainability (ESG) disclosures, selecting industry-relevant topics and metrics, and understanding the framework's uses and limitations for investors and companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary disclosure of financially material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary disclosure guidance of financially material information. SASB Standards provide guidance for companies to disclose financially material sustainability information – meaning companies report on the environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues likely to affect financial performance and firm value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SASB is investor-focused: disclosures should target ESG issues likely to affect financial performance and enterprise value. The framework is voluntary (companies choose whether and how to disclose). SASB is not intended as a comprehensive impact accounting system for all stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry-based standards (77 industries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards are industry-based, with 77 industries represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards vary by industry to account for the subset of ESG issues most relevant to financial performance within each industry. Use the industry-specific standard to ensure reporting covers those topics deemed most material for comparability across peers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize disclosure topics into five issue areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure topics are organized into five issue areas... Environment, Social Capital, Human Capital, Business Model & Innovation, and Leadership & Governance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within each issue area there are General Issue Categories that are industry-agnostic (e.g., under Human Capital: Labor Practices; Employee Health & Safety; Employee Engagement, Diversity, & Inclusion). Use these categorizations to structure reporting and to map specific metrics to broader ESG domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select relevant industry topics via Materiality Finder
rubrics_metrics.description: After selecting the relevant industry for a company, SASB displays the subset of issue categories deemed materially relevant in that industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SASB's Materiality Finder (or the industry standard snapshot) to identify which of the disclosure topics are materially relevant for your industry before preparing disclosures; report on the subset shown as materially relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accounting metrics, technical protocols, and activity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SASB standard provides disclosure topics, accounting metrics, technical protocols and activity metrics that are specifically identified to better manage and communicate financially material sustainability information to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate disclosure topics into the standard's specified accounting metrics and follow the technical protocols so that reported data are comparable, auditable, and meaningful for investment analysis. Include activity metrics to contextualize performance indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SASB to develop ESG strategy and competitive advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies can develop better ESG strategies around material issues and seek ways to outperform their competitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting SASB can help firms focus on material issues, standardize reporting processes recognized by investors, and identify areas for operational or strategic improvement to gain competitive advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enable investor comparability within an industry ('apples-to-apples')
rubrics_metrics.description: Investors can compare ESG disclosures between companies in a common industry on an “apples-to-apples” basis, helping to realize better long-term portfolio performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investors should compare companies using the same industry standard and the same SASB metrics; companies should publish the SASB metrics and protocols to facilitate cross-company comparisons and investment decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with complementary frameworks (e.g., TCFD, EU NFRD)
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB itself is not a mandatory disclosure under any comprehensive reporting framework. However, other frameworks do generally recognize SASB as a suitable disclosure compliance standard. For example, the Task Force on Climate-Related Financial Disclosures (TCFD) has referenced SASB as an appropriate framework for implementing TCFD guidelines, and the European Union’s Non-Financial Reporting Directive has developed supplementary material for how to best integrate SASB into its reporting frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When implementing TCFD or responding to regional reporting directives, use SASB disclosures where appropriate as an accepted way to meet investor-materiality and climate/disclosure guidance. Consult supplementary materials for integration tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define WHAT and RISK dimensions of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB helps identify the most materially important impact outcomes and risks a company should manage. Considering the five dimensions of impact, SASB helps define the WHAT dimension, particularly with its focus on material impacts by industry. SASB also has its own industry guide to the SDGs that can be used by investors to provide evidence for their SDG mapping decisions. In addition to WHAT, SASB can also be used to define RISK dimensions. SASB provides information about the likelihood of risks occurring across different impact categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SASB to map which impacts (WHAT) matter financially and to assess the likelihood/severity of associated risks (RISK). Leverage SASB's SDG mapping guide to align disclosures with SDG objectives where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate SASB with other impact tools (e.g., IRIS+)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other impact reporting frameworks have drawn linkages to SASB. Impact tools, such as the Global Impact Investing Network’s (GIIN’s) impact management and measurement tool IRIS+, have specific guidance for how to use SASB and IRIS+ in coordination to better inform investment decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For broader impact or impact-investing use cases, integrate SASB metrics with IRIS+ or other tools to combine financial-materiality-focused disclosures with broader impact measurement and management practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: FSA Credential for professionals (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: SASB manages the Fundamentals of Sustainability (FSA) Credential. The FSA Credential is designed for professionals to learn and demonstrate their understanding of SASB standards and the link between financially material sustainability information and enterprise value. Individuals must pass both the Level I and Level II exam to earn the FSA Credential. The FSA Credential is not required to perform SASB disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations can encourage staff to obtain the FSA to demonstrate SASB competency, but credentialing is optional and not a compliance requirement for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance: SASB now under the ISSB
rubrics_metrics.description: Consolidation of standards, frameworks, and guidance is happening, and SASB is now under the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB). In June 2021 SASB and the International Integrated Reporting Council (IIRC) merged to form the Value Reporting Foundation (VRF). Further, in 2022 the IFRS Foundation consolidated with the Value Reporting Foundation. This merger followed commitments after COP26 to consolidate sustainability disclosure initiatives in support of the IFRS Foundation’s new International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB). The ISSB now governs SASB Standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting teams and auditors should be aware of ISSB governance and related consolidation when aligning disclosure practices and when tracking future updates to SASB standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: Voluntary disclosure without evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary disclosure without evaluation. The choice of industry or multiple industries, the application of standards within that industry, and the choices of whether to disclose reports and where to disclose reports is entirely up to the company to determine and perform. SASB does not offer compliance evaluations or certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because SASB does not provide third-party compliance verification, companies should consider independent assurance if external validation of disclosures is required or desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: Focus on financially material impacts, not full sustainability reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures focus on only financially material impacts. SASB is not intended to be a comprehensive set of standards for full sustainability or impact reporting. The industry-specific standards identify the issues deemed most financially material, without necessarily considering how certain issues could affect a broader set of stakeholders (beyond owners and investors) in non-financial ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SASB alongside other frameworks (e.g., GRI, IRIS+) when comprehensive stakeholder or environmental/social impact reporting is required; be explicit about the investor-materiality scope when publishing SASB-based reports.
